body.statement: In the unrestricted fixed-population problem on \(2J\) units with potential outcomes in a known bounded interval, minimization over all assignment laws and all measurable estimators is attained by independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment together with the nonlinear Bayes rule generated by a least-favourable endpoint prior. In particular, for binary outcomes this procedure attains \(r^{\mathrm U}_{2J}\).

source.verbatim_statement: A minimax procedure is independent random assignment. Restrict the transformed parameter space to vertices (Aᵢ,Cᵢ)∈{0,1}² for every i. Let d∗ be a minimax rule and π∗ a least-favorable prior. They form a saddle point.

attestation.note: Primary arXiv v3 PDF, Theorem 1 on printed page 8 and Appendix A.4 on printed pages 18–20, downloaded 2026-09-11. The three consecutive source excerpts verify independent Bernoulli assignment, endpoint restriction for the lower bound, and the least-favorable-prior Bayes saddle.
